gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch is a large, multi-faceted change that introduces tonal detection (new tonal_detector.c/h), a morphed noise profile system replacing the discrete noise_reduction_mode selector, a new MINIMUM noise estimator type (mode 4), new utility functions (smooth_spectrum, interpolate_spectrum_gaps, get_morphed_profile), renames blocks_averaged to block_count throughout, removes several deprecated API functions, fixes a bug in critical_bands.c (opus_bands typo and off-by-one), and changes the noise_floor_manager_apply signature. The patch is internally consistent and addresses the stated issue of tonal detection and multiple noise reduction modes.
base_vs_gold_expectation: Base + test patch will fail to compile because the test patch references struct fields (aggressiveness, tonal_reduction) and functions (specbleach_get_noise_profile_block_count_for_mode, specbleach_2d_get_noise_profile_block_count_for_mode, noise_floor_manager_apply with new signature) that only exist after the gold patch. Gold + test patch should compile and pass all tests. The verifier correctly distinguishes between the two states via compilation failure.

No test for the new MINIMUM noise estimator type behavior (mode 4)
No test for the was_learning state transition logic
No test for the critical_bands.c bug fix (opus_bands -> octave_bands typo, off-by-one fix)
Tests primarily verify API surface changes compile rather than testing new algorithmic behavior
too_broad_risks: Full test suite (meson test) runs all 20+ tests including unrelated ones (FFT, whitening, STFT latency, etc.) which could fail for unrelated reasons
Audio file regression tests depend on reference test data files being present and correct

Tests require exact function names: specbleach_get_noise_profile_block_count_for_mode (not blocks_averaged_for_mode or any alternative)
Tests require exact noise_floor_manager_apply signature with tonal_reduction_amount and tonal_mask parameters in specific positions
Tests hardcode mode range 1-4 (MINIMUM = 4) - alternative implementations with different mode numbering would fail
Tests define ROLLING_MEAN = 1 constant matching gold implementation's enum values
An alternative implementation that achieves the same functional goals (tonal detection, multiple reduction modes) but uses different API names or parameter structures would completely fail

Meson 0.61.2 is available - compatible with project requirements

Gold patch spans ~1450 lines across 18 files including 2 new files, header refactoring, algorithm changes, and bug fixes
Test patch modifies 8 test files with 44+ references to gold-specific API names (aggressiveness, tonal_reduction, block_count_for_mode)
Zero grep hits for core new features: tonal_detector, morphed_profile, smooth_spectrum, interpolate_spectrum, noise_estimation_finalize, MINIMUM, detect_tonal

summary: The instance has significant quality issues. The instruction is a two-line PR title providing no actionable implementation guidance for a 1450-line, 18-file patch. Tests are heavily coupled to the gold implementation's exact API naming (44+ hardcoded references to specific field/function names), meaning any reasonable alternative implementation would fail. Core new features (tonal detection, morphed profiles, spectrum smoothing, MINIMUM estimator, critical_bands bug fix) have zero direct test coverage - tests only verify the API surface compiles. The category is mislabeled as 'debugging'. While the pass/fail mechanism works (base+tests won't compile, gold+tests should), the combination of vague instructions and implementation-coupled tests makes this instance unsuitable for evaluating whether a candidate truly solved the problem vs simply reverse-engineering the expected API.
